## Overview

-   **Input:** `results/DE_R_vs_NR_all.csv` and
    `results/processed_shared.rds` (written by RQ1.1.qmd)
-   **Output:** figures in `results/figures/` and tables
    `results/gsea_*.csv`
-   **AI disclosure:** AI was used to help define the settings,
    aesthetics and formatting of the plots and to fix bugs.

```{r packages}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(fgsea)
  library(msigdbr)
  library(pheatmap)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(data.table)
})

set.seed(22123)
dir.create("results/figures", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 12))
pal     <- c(NR = "#7F7F7F", R = "#D55E00")
dir_pal <- c("up in R" = "#D55E00", "down in R" = "#0072B2")
```

## 1. Load the shared outputs of script 01

```{r load}
# Load the DESeq2 results and remove gene without name
de       <- read.csv("results/DE_R_vs_NR_all.csv")
de <- de[!is.na(de$gene) & de$gene != "", ]  
shared   <- readRDS("results/processed_shared.rds")
vst      <- shared$vst
clinical <- shared$clinical

# Keep only the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and split them into up/down in R
sig <- subset(de, direction != "not significant")
up  <- sig[sig$direction == "up in R", ]
dn  <- sig[sig$direction == "down in R", ]

#number of DEGs in each direction
cat("DEGs: up in Responders =", nrow(up), "| down in Responders =", nrow(dn), "\n")
```

## 2. Heatmap of selected DEGs

2 Heatmaps of the top 20 up and top 20 down DEGs by adjusted p-value. In
both heatmaps, genes (rows) are ordered by hierarchical clustering:
genes that are high and low in the same patients are placed next to each
other.

The two heatmaps differ only in how the patients (columns) are ordered:
a) **Ordered**: by response: responders first, then non-responders, b)
**Clustered**: patients are grouped by the similarity of their
expression, without using their response labels.

```{r heatmaps}
#Top 20 Up/down genes
n_each    <- 20
top_genes <- c(head(up$gene[order(up$padj)], n_each),
               head(dn$gene[order(dn$padj)], n_each))

# Z-score each gene across patients (relative high/low) and cap at ±3 so a few extreme samples do not wash out the colour scale
zscore <- function(m, cap = 3) {
  z <- t(scale(t(m)))
  pmin(pmax(z, -cap), cap)
}

#Plot anotations and colors
ann_row    <- data.frame(Direction = ifelse(top_genes %in% up$gene, "up in R", "down in R"),
                         row.names = top_genes)
ann_colors <- list(Response = pal, Direction = dir_pal)
hm_colors  <- colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"))(101)
hm_breaks  <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 102)

# (a) Patients ordered by response (R first)
ord <- order(clinical$BOR, decreasing = TRUE)
mat <- zscore(vst[top_genes, ord])
hm1 <- pheatmap(mat,
         cluster_rows = TRUE, cluster_cols = FALSE,
         gaps_col = sum(clinical$BOR == "R"),
         show_colnames = FALSE, fontsize_row = 7,
         annotation_col = data.frame(Response = clinical$BOR[ord], row.names = colnames(mat)),
         annotation_row = ann_row, annotation_colors = ann_colors,
         color = hm_colors, breaks = hm_breaks,
         main = "Top 20 up + top 20 down DEGs (VST, z-score per gene)",
         filename = "results/figures/heatmap_DEGs_by_response.png",
         width = 9, height = 8)

# (b) Patients clustered by expression: do responders group together on their own?
mat2 <- zscore(vst[top_genes, ])
hm2 <- pheatmap(mat2,
         cluster_rows = TRUE, cluster_cols = TRUE,
         show_colnames = FALSE, fontsize_row = 7,
         annotation_col = data.frame(Response = clinical$BOR, row.names = colnames(mat2)),
         annotation_row = ann_row, annotation_colors = ann_colors,
         color = hm_colors, breaks = hm_breaks,
         main = "Same genes, patients clustered",
         filename = "results/figures/heatmap_DEGs_clustered.png",
         width = 9, height = 8)
```

```{r show-heatmaps}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 8
# Draw the two heatmaps 
grid::grid.newpage(); grid::grid.draw(hm1$gtable)
grid::grid.newpage(); grid::grid.draw(hm2$gtable)
```

## 3. Gene set enrichment analysis (fgsea)

All tested genes are ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (positive =
higher in R). GSEA uses the full ranked list without a significance
cut-off, which helps with only 25 responders. Two MSigDB collections
were used: **GO:BP** (collapsed to reduce redundant gene sets) and
**Hallmark** (50 broad, curated gene sets designed to avoid redundancy).
For the top Hallmark sets we also list the leading-edge genes: the genes
that drive each set's enrichment.

```{r gsea}
# Rank all genes by the DESeq2 Wald statistic 
ranks <- setNames(de$stat, de$gene)
ranks <- sort(ranks, decreasing = TRUE)
cat("Genes in the ranked list:", length(ranks), "\n")

# Get gene sets from MSigDB  and convert them to the list format needed by fgsea
gene_sets_h  <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "H")           
gene_sets_h  <- split(x = gene_sets_h$gene_symbol, f = gene_sets_h$gs_name)         
gene_sets_bp <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "C5", subcollection = "BP")
gene_sets_bp <- split(x = gene_sets_bp$gene_symbol, f = gene_sets_bp$gs_name)

# Run GSEA (fgsea) for Hallmark and GO:BP
set.seed(22123)
gsea_h  <- fgsea(pathways = gene_sets_h,  stats = ranks,
                 minSize = 15, maxSize = 500, nPermSimple = 10000)
set.seed(22123)
gsea_bp <- fgsea(pathways = gene_sets_bp, stats = ranks,
                 minSize = 15, maxSize = 500, nPermSimple = 10000)

# Summary: how many gene sets were tested and how many are significant
gsea_summary <- function(res, name) {
  sig_res <- res[padj < 0.05]
  cat(sprintf("%-8s gene sets tested: %d | padj < 0.05: %d (higher in R: %d, higher in NR: %d)\n",
              name, nrow(res), nrow(sig_res),
              sum(sig_res$NES > 0), sum(sig_res$NES < 0)))
}
gsea_summary(gsea_h,  "hallmark")
gsea_summary(gsea_bp, "gobp")

# Collapse overlapping GO:BP terms into independent main pathways 
set.seed(22123)
collapsed <- collapsePathways(gsea_bp[order(pval)][padj < 0.05],gene_sets_bp, ranks)
bp_main   <- gsea_bp[pathway %in% collapsed$mainPathways]

# Show the 15 most significant Hallmark gene sets
knitr::kable(head(gsea_h[order(padj), .(pathway, NES, padj = signif(padj, 2), size)], 15),
             digits = 3, caption = "Top 15 Hallmark gene sets")

# Show the 15 most significant collapsed GO:BP gene sets (for comparison with Hallmark)
knitr::kable(head(bp_main[order(padj), .(pathway, NES, padj = signif(padj, 2), size)], 15),
             digits = 3, caption = "Top 15 GO:BP main pathways (after collapsing)")

# Where does the first immune term appear in the collapsed GO:BP list?
bp_up <- bp_main[NES > 0][order(padj)]
cat("First immune/interferon GO:BP term among those higher in R is at rank",
    which(grepl("INTERFERON|IMMUNE|T_CELL|LYMPHOCYTE", bp_up$pathway))[1], "\n")

# Take the top 5 Hallmark sets higher in R and the top 5 higher in NR
top_h <- rbind(head(gsea_h[NES > 0][order(padj)], 5),
               head(gsea_h[NES < 0][order(padj)], 5))

# Table of the leading-edge genes genes driving enrichement and which of them are DEGs
le_tab <- data.frame(
  pathway         = top_h$pathway,
  NES             = round(top_h$NES, 2),
  padj            = signif(top_h$padj, 2),
  size            = top_h$size,
  n_leading       = lengths(top_h$leadingEdge),
  top_leading     = vapply(top_h$leadingEdge, function(g) paste(head(g, 15), collapse = ", "), ""),
  DEGs_in_leading = vapply(top_h$leadingEdge, function(g) paste(intersect(g, sig$gene), collapse = ", "), ""))
write.csv(le_tab, "results/gsea_hallmark_leading_edge.csv", row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(le_tab[, c("pathway", "NES", "padj", "n_leading", "top_leading")])
```

## 4. GSEA figures

For both Hallmark and GO:BP (collapsed main pathways), we show three
figures: an NES bar plot of the 20 most significant gene sets, a GSEA
table of the top 10 sets higher in each group, and the enrichment curve
of the most significant set. Orange (NES \> 0) = higher in responders;
blue (NES \< 0) = higher in non-responders.

```{r gsea-plots}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6
# Function: bar plot of NES for the 20 most significant gene sets
plot_nes <- function(res, title) {
  top <- head(res[order(padj)], 20)
  top$label <- gsub("_", " ", sub("^HALLMARK_|^GOBP_", "", top$pathway))  # cleaner names
  ggplot(top, aes(x = reorder(label, NES), y = NES, fill = NES > 0)) +
    geom_col() + coord_flip() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#D55E00", "FALSE" = "#0072B2"),
                      labels = c("TRUE" = "higher in R", "FALSE" = "higher in NR"), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Normalized Enrichment Score (NES)", title = title) +
    theme_minimal()
}

# Hallmark: NES bar plot of the top 20 gene sets
p_h <- plot_nes(gsea_h, "Hallmark gene sets (R vs NR)")
ggsave("results/figures/gsea_hallmark_nes.png", p_h, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
p_h

# GO:BP: NES bar plot of the top 20 main pathways 
p_bp <- plot_nes(bp_main, "GO:BP main pathways (R vs NR)")
ggsave("results/figures/gsea_gobp_main_nes.png", p_bp, width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300)
p_bp
```

```{r gsea-tables}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 8
# GSEA table: top 10 Hallmark sets higher in R and top 10 higher in NR
top_up   <- gsea_h[NES > 0][head(order(pval), n = 10), pathway]
top_down <- gsea_h[NES < 0][head(order(pval), n = 10), pathway]
top_tab  <- c(top_up, rev(top_down))
plotGseaTable(gene_sets_h[top_tab], stats = ranks, fgseaRes = gsea_h, gseaParam = 0.5)

# GSEA table: top 10 GO:BP main pathways higher in R and top 10 higher in NR
top_up   <- bp_main[NES > 0][head(order(pval), n = 10), pathway]
top_down <- bp_main[NES < 0][head(order(pval), n = 10), pathway]
top_tab  <- c(top_up, rev(top_down))
plotGseaTable(gene_sets_bp[top_tab], stats = ranks, fgseaRes = gsea_bp, gseaParam = 0.5)
```

```{r gsea-curves}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
# Enrichment curve of the most significant pathway 
top_h_pw  <- gsea_h[order(padj)][1, pathway]
top_bp_pw <- gsea_bp[order(padj)][1, pathway]

p_curve_h <- plotEnrichment(gene_sets_h[[top_h_pw]], ranks) + labs(title = top_h_pw)
p_curve_bp <- plotEnrichment(gene_sets_bp[[top_bp_pw]], ranks) + labs(title = top_bp_pw)

ggsave("results/figures/gsea_curve_top_hallmark.png", p_curve_h,  width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 300)
ggsave("results/figures/gsea_curve_top_gobp.png",     p_curve_bp, width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 300)
p_curve_h
p_curve_bp
```
